title: High-yield overproduction and purification of human aquaporins from Pichia pastoris
protocol: Draw a numbered grid (1–60) on the petri dish of an YPD-agar plate containing 2,000 μg/mL zeocin.
Randomly select 60 colonies from the transformation plate and spot them on the high-zeocin (2,000 μg/mL) using sterile 10 μL pipet tips.
Incubate the plate at 30°C for 2 days.
Select a minimum of 10 colonies that look larger in size than the others for small-scale expression analysis.
Grow selected colonies at small scale in 5 mL buffered complex glycerol (BMGY) medium overnight with shaking at 30°C.
Check the optical density of the culture at 600 nm (OD600).
Transfer volume equivalent to an OD600 of 1 into a new 50 mL Falcon tube containing complex methanol (BMMY) medium to final volume of 5 mL.
Transfer 1 mL of the BMMY-sample into a 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 15,000 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant.
Freeze the cell pellet for later use as the 0 h induced sample in the western blot.
Grow the remaining 4 mL of the BMMY-culture for 24 hours with 200–300 rpm rotation at 30°C.
Check the OD600 of each culture.
Prepare 24 h induction samples for the western blot.
Add 100% methanol to rest of the culture to a final concentration of 0.5% (v/v).
Grow for another 24 hours.
Check the OD600 at 48 hours.
Prepare 48 h induction samples for the Western blot.
Thaw the frozen samples that were collected at different induction time points.
Analyze AQP expression levels by western blot.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 40 μL of 2× SDS loading buffer.
Heat the samples for 5 min at 95°C.
Do not centrifuge the samples after heating to avoid pelleting down the membrane fraction.
Do not vortex the sample to resuspend the pellet; instead, gently pipette up and down 4–5 times before loading on SDS-PAGE.
If desired, isolate a small membrane fraction for analysis by resuspending the thawed cell pellet in 100 μL of breaking buffer.
Place the suspended pellet on ice and add an equal volume of acid-washed glass beads.
Vortex the mixture 8 × 30 s with 30 s incubation on ice between each vortexing cycle.
Centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 10 min in a desktop centrifuge at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh microcentrifuge tube and pellet down the crude membrane by centrifuging at 20,000 × g at 4°C for 1 h.
Alternatively, use a desktop ultracentrifuge (120,000 × g, for 1 h at 4°C) to pellet down the crude membranes.
Resuspend crude membranes in 30 μL of 2× SDS-PAGE loading buffer.
Load 10 μL for SDS-PAGE and follow the same protocol as for the whole cell fraction.
Run the samples on an SDS-PAGE gel using NuPAGE 4%-12% Bis-Tris gels.
Assemble the chamber with the gel according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Fill up the chamber with SDS running-buffer.
Load 10 μL of each sample in each well, leaving one well empty for the protein ladder.
Load 5 μL pre-stained protein ladder in the empty well.
Run the gel at 200 volts for 35 minutes.
Transfer the protein bands from the gel to a nitrocellulose or PVDF blotting membrane using an XCell II Blot Module.
Block the membrane with 5% (w/v) dry milk in TBST for 1 hour at 22°C.
Incubate with primary anti-His monoclonal antibody (5,000× dilution in TBST with 5% dry milk) for 1 hour at 22°C.
Wash the membrane three times for 10 minutes each in TBST.
Incubate the membrane with HRP-conjugated secondary antibody (5,000× dilution in TBST with 5% dry milk) for 1 hour at 22°C.
Wash the membrane three times for 10 minutes each in TBST.
Develop the membrane with ECL Prime Western Blotting Detection Reagent.
Analyze the chemiluminescence using a western blot imaging system.
Compare the intensity of the western blot signal in different clones to identify the one with the highest AQP expression level.
Estimate the expression level by considering the intensity of all bands, including those for multiple oligomeric states and high molecular weight oligomers.
Overproduce human AQPs in P. pastori at large scale.
Streak a single colony from the desired clone on a YPD-agar plate without antibiotics and incubate it for 2 days at 30°C.
Inoculate 100 mL YPD-medium in a 250 mL flask with a swab of cells from the plate.
Grow the inoculated medium at 30°C for 16 hours.
Check OD600, normally it reaches 20–25 after 16 hours.
Prepare 1.5 L Basal Salt Medium (BSM).
Assemble the fermenter according to manufacturer’s instructions, excluding parts that should not be autoclaved.
Pour BSM into the 3 L fermenter jar using one of the free ports.
Autoclave the fermenter vessel with BSM together with accessory tubing, glycerol, an empty 500 mL bottle, and anti-foam solution.
Prepare 100 mL Pichia trace metals (PTM) and sterile filter it using a 0.2 μM Corning® syringe filter.
Store the PTM-solution at 22°C for up to 6 months.
Inoculate the fermenter around 4 pm on day 2.
Connect all tubing, equipment, and bottles containing base, acid, and anti-foam solution to the fermenter according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Calibrate the pH electrode which should be pH 4 and pH 7 before washing it with 70% (v/v) ethanol.
Insert the calibrated pH electrode into the fermenter vessel.
Calibrate the oxygen detector by setting dissolved oxygen (DO) to 0% when disconnected and 100% when reconnected, ensuring a gas flow of 1 L/min and stirring at 500 rpm.
Wash the oxygen detector probe with 70% (v/v) ethanol before inserting it into the fermenter vessel.
Adjust the pH of the BSM to 5 by adding base.
Add 6.5 mL of PTM to BSM.
Inoculate BSM in the fermenter with the 100 mL overnight starter culture.
Set the fermenter parameters (temperature 30°C, pH 5.0–5.1, DO 25%, gas flow 1 L/min, stirring 800–1,500 rpm).
Run the fermenter overnight.
At around 7-8 am the following day, observe and adjust for glycerol consumption.
Feed the culture with additional 200 mL of 50% (v/v) glycerol mixed with 2.4 mL PTM at a medium speed of 10 mL/h, then gradually increase to 27 mL/h while observing DO levels.
Add a few drops of antifoam if excessive foaming occurs.
At around 3 pm, switch off the glycerol feed and wait for a spike in DO to confirm glycerol depletion.
Switch the feed to 99% (v/v) methanol mixed with 4.8 mL PTM at a medium pump speed of 10 mL/h for 20 minutes.
Switch off the methanol feed.
Wait for about 2 hours for a DO spike to appear.
Once seeing the DO spike, switch on the methanol feed at low speed (2 mL/h) to avoid accumulation.
Estimate total use of 400 mL of methanol during 48 hours of induction.
Add 500 μL anti-foam and leave it for the next 16 hours.
If culture is already foaming a lot, switch off the gas.
Wait for the foam to settle and switch the gas back on.
Repeat until the culture can run calmly with both gas and methanol again.
Wait 10 minutes to ensure foaming does not start again.
Continue the methanol feed from Day 4 onwards.
Increase the methanol feed pump speed gradually to 7 mL/h throughout the day.
If turning off the methanol resulted in a DO spike within 30 seconds, switch the methanol feed back to the same speed as before if the spike does not appear in 30 seconds.
Stabilize the DO around 25 and leave it with the same feeding rate for next 16 hours.
Make sure there is enough methanol left in the bottle to last for 16 hours.
Harvest cells after 48 hours of induction (or whatever time point found optimal).
Turn off everything except stirring (500 rpm) and gas flow (1 L/min).
Connect the sample collecting tube.
Transfer the culture into centrifugation flasks.
Centrifuge at 9,000 × g for 30 minutes using 1 L polypropylene bottles to harvest the cells.
Discard the supernatant and spoon the cells into a 2–3 L plastic bag.
Flatten the content and weigh the cells.
Disassemble and clean the fermenter according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Pre-chill the stainless-steel breaking chamber and 200 mL glass beads at -20°C for 1–2 h or overnight.
Prepare 200 mL of breaking buffer and leave it in the fridge or ice-bath.
Weigh 100 g of fresh or frozen cells in a 400 mL glass beaker.
Add 100 mL breaking-buffer to resuspend the cells.
Stir at room temperature for 30 min to thaw and fully mix the cells.
Add 2 mL of 100 mM PMSF, resulting in a final concentration of 2 mM PMSF in the sample.
Fill the ice jacket with ice and assemble the rotor on the rotor base according to manufacturer instructions.
Run the bead beater for 24 × 30 s intervals with 30 s pauses between each run.
Decant the sample carefully into a 500 mL polypropylene centrifuge bottle, avoiding glass beads inclusion as much as possible.
Wash the beads by adding 100 mL breaking-buffer and add this washing solution to the sample.
Centrifuge the sample using a JLA-10,500 rotor at 16,500 × g for 40 min at 4°C to spin down cell debris and unbroken cells.
Transfer the supernatant to several Ti45 ultracentrifuge tubes.
Collect the membranes through ultracentrifugation at 200,000 × g for 1 h at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Estimate the amount of collected membranes by weighing the tubes before and after transferring the pellets to a potter homogenizer.
Wash the membranes by adding 10 mL urea buffer per gram of membrane.
Homogenize until the pellet has been completely suspended in the buffer.
Transfer the homogenized sample to ultracentrifuge Ti45 tubes.
Wash the homogenizer with an additional 3 mL of urea buffer and add this to the tubes.
Centrifuge at 200,000 × g for 2 hours at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Transfer the pellet to the homogenizer.
Weigh the pellet.
Add 10 mL of membrane buffer with added 1 mM PMSF and 2 mM EDTA pH 9 per gram of membrane.
Homogenize the mixture.
Transfer the sample to Ti45 ultracentrifuge tubes.
Wash the homogenizer with membrane buffer.
Centrifuge again at 200,000 × g for 1.5 hours at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Weigh the membrane pellet.
Homogenize in 0.5 mL/g of membrane buffer.
Divide the resuspended membranes into 10 mL aliquots in 15 mL Falcon tubes.
Freeze the aliquoted membranes.
Screen for a suitable detergent by choosing a set of 5-10 detergents and making stock solutions at 2× final solubilization concentration in freshly prepared solubilization buffer.
Thaw frozen membranes if necessary.
Aliquot 30 μL of membrane suspension for each detergent in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 30 μL of the 2× detergent stock solution.
Incubate the tubes at 4°C with gentle shaking for a total duration of 3 h.
Collect 10 μL samples after 1 and 2 h.
Spin down non-solubilized material in a chilled benchtop centrifuge at 15,000 × g and 4°C for 30 min.
Transfer the supernatant to a separate tube.
Mix the supernatant with 10 μL 2× SDS loading buffer.
Add 10 μL 2× SDS loading buffer to the remaining pellet and resuspend it.
Compare the intensity of AQP bands in the supernatant and pellet for each detergent.
Estimate solubilization efficiency with solubilized AQPs found in the supernatant.
Thaw 10 mL of P. pastoris membranes containing human AQP and transfer to a small beaker.
Dropwise add 10 mL of solubilization buffer containing 8% OG (w/v) while stirring gently.
Incubate with gentle stirring for 2 h at 4°C.
Dilute the sample with 30 mL of solubilization buffer.
Transfer diluted sample to ultracentrifuge tubes.
Spin down insolubilized material at 250,000 × g for 45 minutes at 4°C using a Beckman Ti70 rotor.
Dilute the sample immediately after solubilization to reduce detergent concentration.
Collect the supernatant and add imidazole to achieve a final concentration of 10 mM.
Attach a HisTrap HP 5 mL column to an FPLC-system.
Equilibrate the column with 25 mL of buffer-A using a flow rate of 1 mL/min.
Load the sample at 0.8 mL/min onto the column and continue running buffer-A until the baseline returns to zero.
Wash the column with 15 mL of buffer-B at 1 mL/min.
Elute bound proteins with 20 mL of buffer-C at 1 mL/min, collecting 1 mL fractions.
Evaluate imidazole concentration for each new protein experimentally.
Include more steps and imidazole concentrations or run gradient elution protocol.
Analyze fractions by SDS-PAGE.
Pool desired fractions.
Concentrate up to 10 mg/mL using spin concentrator with a molecular weight cut off of 50 kDa.
Reduce centrifugation speed during concentration step.
Pipette sample up and down several times during the concentration step.
Add 10% (v/v) glycerol after purification.
Aliquot purified protein sample.
Flash freeze in liquid nitrogen.
Store aliquoted samples at -20°C or -80°C for future use.
Remove imidazole from the protein sample using a desalting column or proceed directly to size-exclusion chromatography without freezing.
Proceed with size-exclusion chromatography on the same day if proteins are highly sensitive after imidazole elution.
Purify further using size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) after immobilized metal affinity chromatography (IMAC).
Equilibrate a Superdex 200 Increase 10/300 GL column with SEC-buffer.
Inject 500 μL of the concentrated IMAC sample into a 1 mL loop and load onto the SEC column.
Collect eluate in 1 mL fractions during size-exclusion chromatography.
Analyze interesting fractions by SDS-PAGE.
